steps.text: In **Minor-piece endings: same-coloured or opposite-coloured bishops?** you split the two cases. Now stay with **opposite colours**. **Rule of thumb:** one extra pawn usually does not win, because the defending bishop cannot be chased off the colour the pawn needs. **Exception to test:** two passed pawns far apart on different wings. See one, then check the claim yourself.

steps.caption: Opposite-coloured bishops. White has two passed pawns, on the a-file and the f-file. White wins (tablebase).

claims.statement: White wins from the start position.

steps.text: **When the exception holds.** The stronger side has two passed pawns on far-apart files. The defending king and bishop cannot cover both. **When it fails.** Only one passed pawn: in these examples the same setup is drawn. Rule of thumb: ask whether the defender can cover both pawns. Pawns side by side are a different case; check them with the tablebase, not by this rule.

steps.title: Again: the second pawn is the difference

steps.prompt: Before you looked, did you count the passed pawns and check the bishop colours? Which position was the one where you changed your mind?
